Invoicing & payments - AI tools for contractors

Turning completed work into invoices, chasing payment and reconciling the books.

Why this matters Getting paid weeks after the work is done is a cash-flow problem, not an admin problem.

What Invoicing & payments actually involves

Getting paid is a process, not an event. Most late payment in the trades comes from slow invoicing rather than unwilling customers: the work finishes on Friday and the invoice goes out the following week. Taking card payment on site removes most of the problem, and staged billing protects you on larger jobs.

Frequently asked questions

Which invoicing & payments tools are worth trying first?

The three that stand out here are Joist (Solo contractors and small crews who mainly need to quote and get paid), Knowify (Contractors who need to know whether a job actually made money), Housecall Pro (Home service businesses that want one app covering booking through to payment). Start with the one that matches your size and the work you do most, not the one with the longest feature list.

How much does invoicing & payments software cost?

Across the 10 tools on this page, 2 have a free tier and the rest are paid, most of them billed per user per month. Prices move often, so confirm on the vendor site before committing.

Can I try these tools for free?

Yes 鈥?Joist, Workiz all have a free tier, so you can run a few real jobs through them before paying anything.

Should I take card payments on site?

Yes, if your average job is under a few thousand. Getting paid before you leave removes the entire chasing problem, and the processing fee is usually smaller than the cost of one invoice that sits unpaid for a month.
